parsed.explanation: Combined regime exposes an outed visitor at visa, border, facilities and custody with compounding state action: X-markers stopped, document discrepancy can lead to refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal and many subnational facility bans with one documented trespass arrest and men's-ward hold, and documented immigration/prison abuse and care removal. The division adds an upheld minor-care ban, prison-care funding ban, sports ban, surgery-based document rule and no gender-identity anti-discrimination law. Functioning courts and hate-crime coverage mitigate partly—some orders were blocked—but the Supreme Court allowed passport restrictions and the state high court upheld the care ban. No execution or highly likely imprisonment for presence was documented, so severity is below the 0.25 tier despite multiple universal exposures.

entry_documents.exposure: X-marker passports no longer issued; new markers only M/F by birth documents. Visa cable: discrepancy or reasonable doubt requires refusal and added evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation can support permanent lifetime ineligibility. Passports reportedly confiscated/blocked, neighbouring citizens detained over visas, allied advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration. Lifetime fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist. Civil-liberties suit and court challenges remain pending; several related orders were blocked or enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: Visa adjudication precedes travel; a document discrepancy can therefore become refusal, delay or a lasting immigration bar before entry, and can recur at border inspection. Status of foreign X passports at entry is not specifically documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal prisons adopted conversion-therapy model: short haircuts, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; transgender prisoner numbers stopped being reported. Immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. A bathroom trespass arrestee was held 24 hours in men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No visitor-specific custody safeguard, inspection or successful remedy for the reported abuse is documented; litigation over some national orders does not show custody protection operating.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for facilities/documents can escalate into birth-sex ward placement, care interruption and, in immigration custody, documented severe abuse. Bureau non-reporting increases uncertainty rather than safety.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars government-funded single-sex facilities inconsistent with birth sex. Mapped bans cover all government buildings in 10 jurisdictions, schools plus some government buildings in 9, schools only in 3; 6 extend to some private settings and 4 make use criminal in circumstances, including trespass after refusal to depart.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states, 4 other units and the capital district have no ban in mapped categories, but the map warns other sex-definition laws may affect access. This division's specific facilities category is not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rule applies throughout; state law may add criminal trespass and document invalidation. A visitor cannot avoid the exposure by choosing a non-ban state if federal facilities, schools or clinics are involved.

care_services.exposure: Division SAFE Act bans starting puberty blockers/hormones under 18 and all transition surgery for minors, bars Medicaid payment at any age, restricts prison/jail care, and risks provider licence loss and lawsuits up to 15 years. HB 2009 bars prison hormone/surgery funding with no taper. Both upheld/operative; care-ban movement is toward permanence.
care_services.protection: Minors already in treatment may continue under SAFE Act. Some comparable national orders were blocked/withdrawn, but the division ban survived trial, appeal and the state high court in January 2026.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor loses continuity and cannot start hormones/blockers; providers face liability, creating denial/reporting risk for child and guardian. Adult prison-care exposure is resident-facing but shows custody practice.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National policy defines sex as binary birth sex, removes gender-identity materials/policies, bans trans athletes' entry, directs investigation/prosecution over school social transition, and uses 'radical gender ideology' in extremism guidance. May 2026 strategy prioritises neutralising groups described as radically pro-transgender. Division has a care-ban tipline.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism strategy says powers will not target people who merely disagree. Several orders were blocked/enjoined, and gender-identity hate crimes are federally punishable; division hate-crime law explicitly covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing can increase officer discretion at visa, facility and school encounters. The documented phrase is not itself a standalone visitor arrest criterion, and no visitor arrest under counterterrorism powers is documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor is barred from starting blockers/hormones and from surgery, facing provider licence and civil liability; schools through college restrict sports by birth sex. National directives target school facilitation of social transition and DOJ subpoenaed hospital records for minors. Proposed rules would bar public insurance for under-18 care.
minors_guardians.protection: Continuing existing treatment is expressly allowed. SAFE Act sunsets in 2027, but lawmakers seek permanence and a November 2026 ballot initiative would bar care indefinitely; litigation failed at state high court.
minors_guardians.interaction: For a family, adult guardian may be unable to secure lawful continuity, school sports or care without exposing providers, and reporting systems create investigation risk even if the guardian is not the direct defendant.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented. No dated division incident, trans-specific violence rate, denominator or visitor attack is provided; absence is not treated as safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; the division hate-crime statute explicitly covers gender identity. Enforcement outcomes for visitors are not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Paper hate-crime recourse may help after an attack, but public support for birth-sex documents was 66% in a cited 2025 poll, indicating hostility risk without establishing current violence prevalence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Supreme Court allowed passport-marker restrictions in November 2025 and upheld an analogous minor-care ban quoted by the division high court in January 2026. Passport, executive-order and health-rule challenges remain unresolved, so present exposure depends on which measures are operative.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, other injunctions/blocks, legal-aid passport guidance, federal hate-crime law and division hate-crime coverage show courts and remedies are not wholly unavailable, reducing severity below a no-recourse regime.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are strongest against some national executive orders and weakest where the highest courts have now allowed the operative passport and care regimes; that interaction leaves entry and minor-care risks largely unremedied.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case: birth-sex prison housing with frequent assaults, cross-dressing arrests and rare protection. Here custody abuse is documented, but visitor imprisonment is not highly likely, execution is absent, and courts have blocked some measures, placing the case above 0.25.

Similar to this case: passport/phone confiscation, hours-long detention, fines and deferential courts. Here visa refusal/lifetime-ineligibility risk, criminalised facilities, minor-care liability and custody abuse compound, but documented injunctions and hate-crime recourse keep it near, slightly above, 0.35.

Higher than this case: ward placement by document marker delays care but remedies include advocates and ethics review. Here discrepancy can cause refusal or permanent ineligibility, trespass arrest can occur, and minor-care providers face licence loss, so the operative regime is materially harsher.

Much lower than this case: nonbinary passports accepted, trained officers, counsel, tribunal apology and discipline. Here X issuance stopped, discrepancy triggers refusal, and no equivalent visitor remedy is documented, so the case is far below the 0.85 protective tier.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one interacting system, not separable national and division layers. Document discrepancy can trigger visa refusal or a possible lifetime fraud bar; entry/facility checks can trigger criminal trespass and birth-sex placement; detention can trigger care removal and documented abuse; for a minor, care, school and sports rules transfer risk to providers and guardians. Courts, injunctions, hate-crime coverage and grandfathering prevent the lowest tier, but the highest courts have allowed the central passport and analogous care regimes, and many punitive provisions compound rather than cancel. Hence an Elevated-Risk score around 0.40.
